topics.topic: Startup validation rules for installed bindings without operation or port context
questions: Which A08 rule 5 checks apply at startup when this operation has a service and selected instance but no operation name or proposed ports?

Which exact A08 rule 5 checks are ‘checks of the record itself’ at startup, given that rule 5 mixes service-record, capability, selected-instance, proposal-port and operation-specific checks and no operation or proposal ports are supplied here?
Which manifest checks are performed at startup when no operation name or proposed ports are inputs, and in what order are multiple capabilities examined?

judgement.why: This is the same startup manifest-validation question, and neither the relevant passages nor the change affect it.

precedent.topic: Scope of A08 rule 5 validation during installed-instance startup checks
quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
precedent.why: The later notes limit startup validation to credential-bearing services, ordered by service_id, and to top-level service-record checks plus the selected instance's credential-header collision.

topics.topic: Allowed HTTP base URLs and exact request-URL joining behavior
questions: May `api_base_url` contain user information, a path, query or fragment, and exactly how is the request URL and Host authority formed in those cases?
Are base URLs with a path, multiple trailing slashes, user information, a query or a fragment valid, and exactly how are they joined to the declared operation path?

judgement.why: This repeats the unresolved base-URL grammar and joining question on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Accepted API base URL forms, path joining, and resulting HTTP authority
quotes:
the installation selects no instance for the service or that
   instance has no `api_base_url` — one that is not an absolute `http` or
   `https` URL with a host counts as none — or names one required header
   twice, or names one the kernel sets itself (`host`, `accept-encoding`,
   `content-type`, `content-length`, A10 rule 7) other than `host`, which an
   instance may set instead of the kernel (A10 rule 7), names compared without
   regard to case — at send time both are A09 rule 6's `required_header_repeated`
   —, or has a required header whose name is not an HTTP field-name token, or whose value is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or holds a control character — at send time `required_header_invalid`;

The
   URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared
   path, which must start with one `/` and contain no `//`, no `.` or `..`
   segment, no `?` or `#`, and no scheme or host; a `{` or `}` appears only in a
   placeholder, which is one whole segment `{name}` whose name is not empty and
   contains no `{`, `}` or `/`, and no name is a placeholder twice; a path that
   does not is not invocable (A08 rule 3). Placeholder values are percent-encoded so that they
   stay one segment. Nothing else is normalized.

Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
   The host judged here, the one connected to, and for `https` the server name
   sent and verified, are always those of `api_base_url`; a required `Host`
   header (A10 rule 7) changes only the header sent.

`host` — the authority of `api_base_url` exactly as the manifest writes it,
   not normalized (A09 rule 1), unless the instance's required headers name
   `host`, in which case that required header is sent instead, its value
   verbatim, and is the only `host` —, `accept-encoding: identity` (A09 rule 3),
precedent.why: The texts constrain an absolute HTTP(S) URL and simple concatenation but do not close the accepted URL grammar, slash handling, component interaction, or loopback classification.

topics.topic: Length unit used when masking classified failure details
questions: Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode scalar values, characters after replacement and truncation, or another unit?
Is the reported length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, characters after replacement, or the original response bytes?

judgement.why: This is the same failure-detail length-unit question already answered by the later text, with no relevant change.

precedent.topic: Unit and truncation basis of masked failure-detail length
quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
precedent.why: The later notes define the disclosed length as the UTF-8 byte length of the stored, already bounded failure_detail.

topics.topic: Ordering, failure precedence, and cleanup during output post-processing
questions: In what deterministic order are value-size checks, file spooling and target-port deliveries performed, and which status wins when different outputs fail different post-sandbox checks?
In what order are multiple value and file outputs size-checked and spooled, and what files remain when a later output makes the element fail?

quotes: execute_function: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns SandboxResult with the outcome, outputs only for succeeded as PortPayload entries in output port name order (a value as its canonical JSON bytes, a file as its bytes, a many file port as the list of its bytes), resources_used with elapsed wall_time_ms, peak memory_bytes and the output count as output_bytes, failure_detail, and detail_code None except for cleanup_failed.

execute_function_element: [BEHAVIOR] On an outcome other than succeeded the NodeExecutionDraft carries that outcome as status with the SandboxResult detail_code, failure_detail and resources_used, executed the ExecutedImplementation, the input PortRefs and no outputs. On succeeded, each JSON output above the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant concludes contract_violation with detail value_too_large, the SandboxResult's resources_used and no outputs; otherwise JSON outputs are published with put_value_bytes as StoredValues of the port's stored schema (M21: its value_schema, or for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items), and files are published with spool_file under the run, node, map_index, the element's next attempt_number — the count of its NodeExecutions read with ExecutionsOfElement plus one, the number its record is then written under — the port and the list_index for a many port, a RefusedError from spool_file concluding resource_exhausted with the SandboxResult's resources_used, no outputs and no file of that attempt kept.

spool_file: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise RefusedError when the size of content exceeds the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SPOOL_FILE_BYTES_MAX constant, or when the run's spool, counted as the bytes of the files already in it, less a file no SpooledFile record names at this file's position, plus content, would exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SPOOL_RUN_BYTES_MAX constant; on that refusal it removes this file and every file already spooled under the same run_id, producer_node_id, map_index and attempt_number, so nothing of that attempt's files is kept, while files of earlier attempts stay. The attempt_number of the key is the element's next number as the caller read it; spool_file does not assign one.

advance_run: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id; a node is ready when every input port holds its value: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them, constants to their port, and outputs of a concluded succeeded node along every edge whose guard is absent or whose guard port value equals the guard value as canonical JSON text. A mapped node, once selected, takes its elements in list order, executing every element with no concluded record that does not wait, before the next node is selected; a waiting or failed element does not stop the elements after it, and a concluded element is never executed again.

advance_run: [BEHAVIOR] Before a value enters a node it MUST pass fit_port_value against the target port, with the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant for a value and the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SPOOL_FILE_BYTES_MAX constant for a file; a misfit concludes the receiving element contract_violation without running it: runs writes its NodeExecution with executed naming its pinned implementation or binding, the inputs it had with the misfit value among them, no outputs, no resources_used, and started_at and ended_at both the time of the check from kernel_now; the value is not delivered. An element that does not succeed keeps no output: its NodeExecution names none, a value it produced is not stored and the files its attempt spooled are discarded with no SpooledFile record naming them.
judgement.why: The later notes order returned outputs by port name, check all JSON output ceilings before publication, then publish values and files, remove every file of the attempt on a spool-ceiling refusal, and validate target inputs when their nodes are selected.

topics.topic: Retry policy for token-list reads after a failed reread
questions: After a failed re-read clears the valid token list, must every later request retry reading the file even when the restored file has the same digest as the last previously valid file?
After a failed re-read, when is another re-read attempted, especially if readability or permissions are repaired without changing the file bytes?

quotes: current_token_list: [BEHAVIOR] On every call MUST read the configuration file's bytes and compare their SHA-256 with the last read digest; when equal it returns the kept list unchanged (none stays none); when different, or when the file cannot be read, it re-reads the file and applies exactly four checks: the file can be read and parses as a JSON object with owner_token and agent_tokens of the Installation types, every token is at least the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant long, no two tokens are equal, and no two agent tokens have the same name; the new digest becomes the last read digest, and when the file cannot be read the last read digest is cleared, so the next readable bytes are always re-read.

current_token_list: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] When all four checks hold, the re-read's tokens replace the kept list; when any fails the kept list becomes none and the old list is discarded, since it may hold a revoked token; a re-read takes only the token list, and no other field of the kept Installation changes until a restart.
judgement.why: The later notes require a read on every call and clear the saved digest after an unreadable file, ensuring restored readable bytes are revalidated.

topics.topic: Revision-pinned manifest source resolution and failure handling
questions: What kind of source is `manifest_location`, and how must `bindings` resolve and read a file at `manifest_revision` without silently using a working-tree or current-file version?
How does `bindings` obtain the service record for a particular `manifest_revision`, and what exact failures mean that the revision or record is unavailable?

judgement.why: This is the same revision-pinned manifest-source question already answered by the later contract, with no relevant change.

precedent.topic: How bindings reads and verifies service records at a specific manifest revision
quotes:
8. **The manifest at a revision**: `manifest_location` is a directory inside a
git repository and `manifest_revision` a commit of it; `bindings` reads
`<service_id>.json` of that directory at that commit as a git object, never
from the working tree, so a record changes only with the configured revision
(A08 rules 1 and 6).
precedent.why: The later contract requires reading the manifest record as a Git object at the configured commit, never from the working tree.
